title: operator-conntrack-depletion-during-onprem-rolling-upgrades
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple on-prem customers reported rolling upgrade failures for the operator/helm post-upgrade reconciliation. Investigation shows short bursts of node-level conntrack table exhaustion during upgrade traffic patterns (kube-proxy, host networking, and helm-operator’s rollout probes). When conntrack entries spike, control plane requests time out and Helm upgrades fail to complete, leaving CRs in a 'Pending' state and triggering customer escalations.

Scope: Affects Private/VPC on-prem clusters running our operator (v1.18.x and v1.19.x variants) with default host networking conntrack limits. Observed across three escalations (customer A, B, C) with clusters sized 3-7 nodes. Not observed in Hosted clusters.

Observed failure mode: During a rolling upgrade we see a spike in short-lived NAT/conntrack entries from probe traffic + init containers. Node conntrack table becomes saturated, kernel drops new connections briefly, kubelet/kube-proxy health checks and helm-operator helm client calls fail with timeout or ECONNRESET. Helm release stuck in post-upgrade hook, operator retries, increasing probe rate and making the situation worse.

Root cause hypothesis: Operator rollout combined with heavier-than-expected probe/retry patterns + host-level applications (customer infra) generated bursty ephemeral connections that exceed conntrack_max. Default sysctl settings on affected AMIs/OS images are too low for our upgrade patterns.

Immediate mitigation (customer-facing): 1) Run sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 on affected nodes as a hotfix; 2) Temporarily increase kube-proxy conntrack-*-timeout settings where supported; 3) If conntrack cannot be increased, pause operator rollouts and perform node-by-node manual upgrades with longer intervals.

Proposed engineering fix: 1) Ship operator hotfix v2026.03.2 that reduces probe aggressiveness during upgrades and applies exponential backoff on helm client retries; 2) Add preflight check to onprem install/upgrade that warns/auto-tunes conntrack sysctl (with opt-out) and outputs remediation commands; 3) Add a post-upgrade validation step that detects conntrack saturation and triggers safe rollback/pausing of rollout; 4) Update runbook and customer KB with clear remediation steps and kubelet/kube-proxy tuning guidance.

Rollback and release plan: - Cut hotfix release on branch release/onprem-2026.03 - Include probe/backoff changes + preflight check. - Canary rollout to internal staging and 2 low-risk customers (customer D, internal QA). - If canary good, coordinate with SEs to apply API-side feature flag for immediate customer enablement and schedule automated rollout for remaining customers.

Testing: Add e2e scenario that simulates high ephemeral connection churn during upgrades (using load-generator) and verify operator does not cause conntrack depletion. Add unit tests for backoff logic.

Monitoring & alerts: Create dashboards: conntrack usage per-node, helm-operator helm client error rates, operator rollout-time histogram. Add pager alert if conntrack usage > 85% for 3 consecutive minutes during upgrade window.

Documentation: Update onprem upgrade checklist with explicit conntrack preflight and remediation script. Publish KB article with step-by-step commands and explanation for customers and Solutions Eng.

Success criteria: - No new escalations for the same root cause within 30 days for customers on hotfix release. - Preflight catches >90% of vulnerable clusters during install/upgrade. - Automated rollback/pausing reduces failed rollouts by 95% in simulated tests.
